question_type: Arithmetic mean of calendar-year 'Sales' over five years from an 'All Series Combined' sales-and-redemptions table

opus_divergence.what_opus_did: Found that every 1954 issue has two tables with the identical title 'Table 2.- Sales and Redemptions by Periods, All Series Combined': one under UNITED STATES SAVINGS BONDS and one under TREASURY SAVINGS NOTES. It chose the Treasury savings notes table. Its reasons: it read the question's parenthetical '(U.S. Treasury)' as pointing to 'Treasury savings notes', and 1949-1953 are exactly the notes' individual calendar sales years. It computed the savings-bonds mean as an alternative but did not submit it.
opus_divergence.what_right_glm_did: none and prompt used the Sales column (calendar-year rows) of the U.S. savings bonds 'All Series Combined' Table 2, which is the first table with that title in each issue. Neither weighed the notes table. none also read '(U.S. Treasury)' as a source attribution ('maybe source Treasury Bulletin').
opus_divergence.evidence: Opus worklog Step 2, Step 4 and the 'Decision' section; solution.json decisions[0]; treasury_bulletin_1954_02.txt:1969-1994 (bonds) vs :2381-2435 (notes). GLM none: [19] summed the Series E/H and F/G/J/K panels, [27] treated the parenthetical as a source, [38]-[41] read bonds Table 2 in 1954_03. GLM prompt: [11]-[15], and [19]-[22], where a vintage scan returned two same-titled table starts per issue but only the first (bonds) table was opened.

reviewer_flag: Verdict UNCERTAIN. No numeric error. The reviewer called bonds vs notes a genuine ambiguity and computed the bonds alternative, but kept the notes choice, citing the '(U.S. Treasury)' wording, the notes' source line ('Office of the Treasurer of the U.S.') and the notes' sales years.
right_by_principled_choice_or_luck: Mostly luck or salience. The right arms never considered the Treasury savings notes table: prompt's scan at [19] listed two table starts per issue, but it opened only the first. They reached savings bonds because it is the first and most prominent 'all series' table, and 'series' conventionally means the savings-bond series E-K. The one principled element is none's reading of '(U.S. Treasury)' as a source tag at [27].
wrong_glm_arms_same_as_opus: No. The wrong arm (cards) chose the savings-bonds table, like the right arms. It failed by mixing sources across cells: it took 1949 from the dedicated Table 2 but kept 1951 from its earlier sum of the Series E/H and F/G/J/K panels ([16] vs [25]-[34]), so its mean is slightly off (within 0.1%). The fix would have been to take every cell from one table.
lesson_for_harness: When two tables share an identical title, default to the primary and most prominent one: the first in the issue, whose meaning of the key noun ('series') is the standard one. Treat parenthetical qualifiers like '(U.S. Treasury)' as source attribution unless they literally reproduce a table or section label. Opus's error was over-reading a parenthetical as a disambiguator. For the weaker actor, the useful mechanism is a same-title-table detector (TOOL/CHECK) that lists every table with the identical title in the issue, plus a fixed tie-break rule, so the choice is deliberate rather than accidental. A single-source CHECK (all cells of a series come from one table and one vintage) would have caught cards' failure.
notes: The graded answer is the alternative Opus computed and recorded, and the reviewer computed it too. The relative gap between the two readings is about 0.14%. Both tables are vintage-stable from 1954 to 1956, so vintage was not a factor. Across Q50 and Q83, Opus's errors come from interpreting question wording away from the most salient or literal reading, and the reviewer endorsed the over-interpretation both times.
